Commentary.Commentary: Right then! That is it from this game. The next one is a must win for Zimbabwe and they have to come up with better plans. The second ODI is on 31st August at 5.10 am IST (11.40 pm GMT, the previous day). Do join us for the build up as well. Cheers!

Cameron Green is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his maiden five-wicket haul. Green says he needed to realize what the wicket is doing and then bowl accordingly. Adds he wanted to hit the back of the length area and it worked. Informs he enjoys fishing over golf.

Regis Chakabva, the skipper of Zimbabwe says he felt the wicket was tricky, they though did not have enough on the board. Mentions they did not finish well with the bat and with the ball, the start was not that great. Ends by saying they need to work on the positives and hope to do well in the next game.

Aaron Finch, the skipper of Australia says the ball was doing a bit throughout and they finished well with the ball. Mentions the preparation is same against every team and they were well prepared for this game. Reckons Mitchell Starc is one of the best bowlers in the world and his contribution has been exceptional and Green was outstanding and it is great he got a fifer.
...Presentation coming up...
Earlier, Zimbabwe were bundled out to an under-par score thanks to Cameron Green's fifer and Adam Zampa's three wickets. Australia fancied a win and in the end, they won comfortably by 5 wickets.

Zimbabwe can be pleased with how they bowled! Especially Sikandar Raza and Ryan Burl who were outstanding. The latter ended with three and gave Zimbabwe the slightest of chances. However, they just did not have enough on the board.

Then the Aussie batters batted with intent. Steven Smith was the anchor and the others played their shots. There were a couple of decent innings with David Warner's fifty giving the perfect start but Smith was the mainstay with a half ton. There was a period when Australia might have felt a little pressure when they lost three quickly but Glenn Maxwell and Steven Smith ensured no more wickets fell and took their side over the line.

A comfortable win in the end for the hosts and they go 1-0 up in the three-match series! The victory however was set up in the first innings itself as Cameron Green's fifer saw Zimbabwe being bundled out for a low score.
SIX! Two big hits and Maxwell finishes off in style! A length ball on the pads. Glenn Maxwell whacks it over deep square leg for a biggie. Australia win by 5 wickets.
SIX! Just 6 needed now! Short of a length and around off. Maxwell pulls it high over deep square leg for a biggie.
On a length and around off. Smith taps it to covers for a single.
On a length and around off. Smith tucks it to mid-wicket for one more. 13 runs needed now.
Wide! Angles one down the leg side. Smith looks to flick but misses.
A fuller ball, outside off. Smith mistimes his drive back to the bowler.
This is way outside off. Smith lets it go.
Wide! A full ball, way down the leg side, Smith leaves it alone.
Angles a length ball on middle. Smith blocks it out.
On a length and outside off. Smith punches it to covers.
This is full and outside off. Smith looks to drive but gets beaten on the inside edge.
FOUR! This game is nearing its end! Maxwell in full flow here. He brings out the reverse sweep, it is a full toss outside off. He hits it down to the third man fence.
FOUR! That is a poor delivery! Short and on the body, this is pulled past short fine leg for a boundary.
SIX! Short side and Maxwell clears it with ease. On middle, Maxwell brings out the slog sweep, it goes over the square leg fence.
On off, this is pushed down to long off for one.
Another one outside off, not played at.
WIDE! Well wide outside off, left alone.
Gives it air, this lands outside off, it is driven through covers for one.
On middle, kept out.
On off, this is pushed towards cover for one.
Fired on the pads, Maxwell looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
FOUR WIDES! This lands on leg stump and turns away. Smith leaves it alone. The keeper fails to take it and it goes down to fine leg for three.
Another two as this is also played through point.
On off, this is guided past point for two.
On middle, defended.
FOUR! Up and over! Maxwell off the mark in style. That is a serious shot. On a wicket where the ball is turning. He lifts this left spinner on middle over mid on for a boundary.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Australia 5 down all of a sudden and still need above 40. Zimbabwe have a little sniff here. Burl gets another one. This is pushed through outside off. Marsh looks to cut but this is a little too full. It goes off the toe-end and it is taken by the keeper. Another wicket quickly and it is game on here.
Commentary.Howout: c Regis Chakabva b Ryan Burl

Commentary.Commentary: TWO! Marsh cuts this one past point now and bags a couple.
Tossed up outside off, left alone.

Tossed up on off, kept out.

Well stopped! On off, this is pushed towards cover. The fielder dives to his right and makes a half stop. A single.
Flatter and on off, blocked.
On middle, this is worked to square leg.
This lands and spins away. Blocked.
On off, this is pushed to cover.
Shorter ans outside off, spins away. Stoinis looks to cut but is beaten.
Flatter and on middle, defended.

A single to end then! On off, this is pushed through covers for one.

Wide of the fielder in the deep! Tossed up on off, Stoinis lifts it over covers for two.
On off, this lands and turns away. Blocked.
Flatter and on off, defended.

OUT! TAKEN! Burl has a wicket. Tossed up nicely, it is around off. Carey looks to go over long on. He actually plays a half hearted shot. It goes towards the fielder there and Victor Nyauchi takes it on the second attempt.
Commentary.Howout: c Victor Nyauchi b Ryan Burl

Flatter ball, around off. Defended out. Australia need another 73 runs to win.
Full ball, angling on middle. Carey works it to long on for one.
FOUR! Tossed up on off. Carey gets inside the line and paddles it past short fine leg for a boundary.
Two wides! Fuller and sliding down. Smith misses his flick. The keeper gets a bit of glove on it and gives away a single.
Slower now, outside off. Blocked again.
Full and on midde. Smith again makes a solid block.
Flatter and on middle. Blocked out.
FOUR! Really well played! Cheeky from Carey! A full toss on middle. Carey reverse sweeps it through backward point for a boundary.
Outside off, guided to sweeper cover for a single.
Full ball, outside off, driven to covers.
Too full and around off. Smith flicks it in the gap, through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Tossed up, around off. Blocked out.
FOUR! Too full and outside off. Smith drags and hits it over mid on for a boundary.
Turn and bounce there! Tossed up, outside off, it spins away and beats the outside edge of Carey as he looks to drive.
A googly, shorter and on midde, Smith nudges it to mid-wicket and takes a quick single.
Tossed up on middle. Smith punches it to mid on.
Flatter, slower and outside off, slapped to deep cover for a single.
This is full and on middle, pushed to covers.

OUT! BOWLED 'EM! This time David Warner has to walk back! Much-needed wicket for the visitors! Raza serves a floated delivery, full and angling in around middle. Warner pre-meditates and goes for a big heave but misses and the ball rattles the stumps. Australia need 93 more runs to win. A fine innings comes to an end.

IN THE AIR AND FALLS SAFELY! Warner living a charmed life right now! Shorter, quicker and on middle. Warner looks to work on the leg side but closes the face of the bat too early. He gets a top edge and the ball lobs away from mid on for a single.
Around off, pushed through covers for a single.
Again Burl sees Warner lining up a reverse hit and he changes his line and serves a full ball. Warner works it away for a single.
FOUR! Smashed away! Floated full ball, outside off. Warner drives it through covers for four more.
Tossed up, around middle. Warner stays back to defend.
A flighted ball on leg. Warner flicks it to mid-wicket.
A googly, full and on middle. Smith bunts it to square leg.
Again Smith can't beat the fielder as this time he pulls to square leg.
Drops it short and on middle, pulled hard but straight to mid-wicket.
FOUR! 100 up for the Aussie! Tossed up, just outside off. Smith opens his body and lofts it over extra cover for a boundary.
Raza serves it full and on the pads, flicked to square leg.
Shorter and around middle, nudged to square leg.
A googly, shorter and outside off. Warner cuts it to short third man. Australia need another 104 runs to win.
Flighted, full ball, outside off. Smith drives it to deep cover for only a single.
Quicker, shorter and on middle. Smith nudges it to mid-wicket.
Flatter and on middle. Smith keeps it out.
Burl sees Warner go for a reverse hit and he serves a yorker around middle. Warner was quick to jam it out. A single in the end.
Tossed up, around off. Warner pushes it to covers.

To walk or not? What does Adam Gilchrist think about this? Thoughts go back to that 2003 World Cup semifinal against Sri Lanka, where the umpire did not give him out, yet he walked. In this rare, very rare scenario, Warner thought he was out and started to walk back before the official decision could be given. But then, when he realized that technology was not ready to deprive Aussie fans of a Warner blitzkrieg, he walked back to the crease. Now, the question to be asked here is - If Davey felt he was out, why did he do a U-turn? Might be interesting to see what he actually said to Regis Chakabva, the Zimbabwe keeper. Chakabva was all smiles and one could actually see Warner mouthing - ' I HEARD A NOISE.' So, just to give, say 5 percent benefit of doubt, DW did not think he edged it. He just felt that there was a noise and there was no other place from where it could come, apart from the outside edge. My eyesight is not the best but a look the replays does suggest that there was a deviation, along with the noise. Don't think there was turn. The argument will go on regarding the spirit of cricket but if there is something called as Lady Luck, it is surely smiling on Warner.
Full ball, on off. Smith prods to defend.
Flatter ball, outside off. Smith works it to backward point.
This one lands on middle and turns away from the batter. Smith tickles it to short fine leg.
On the pads. Smith keeps it out.
Fifty for Warner! 35th ODI fifty for the Aussie opener! Class as always! Flatter and outside off. Warner punches it through point for a single.
SIX! Warner moves to 49! Short ball on middle. Warner pulls it off the back foot over mid-wicket for a biggie.
Short one on middle. Warner works it to third man for a single.
FOUR! Thumped! This is full and outside off. Warner smashes it past the diving mid off fielder for four.
On middle, flicked behind square on the leg side for a couple.
Full and on off, pushed to mid off.
A bouncer on middle. Warner leaves it.
Shorter and outside off, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.

A huge appeal for caught behind and the finger stays down. The keeper, Regis Chakabva is convinced and takes it upstairs. There is definitely a noise when the ball goes past the bat and the replay seems to show a deflection. In fact, DAVID WARNER IS WALKING BACK. But hang on. Drama! Hot Spot shows NOTHING. Time for Snicko and that shows nothing either! Boy o boy. What does Warner do now? Does he continue walking? No, he is ready to accept the new elixir of life. He is walking back to the crease, with a sheepish smile. The Zimbabwe players are in disbelief. Technology doesn't show the same thing. Well, not out it is!
On middle, pushed through point for a single.

Dropped! Shorter, width on offer, outside off, Warner cuts it uppishly towards point and Tadiwanashe Marumani there tries to take over his head but palms it over for a single. Should have been taken. A regulation catch.
FOUR! Pulled away! Drops it short and on off. Warner gets low and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a boundary.
Shorter and on off. Smith punches off the back foot to long on for one.
Tossed up, around off. Warner drops it to cover for one.

Drinks! Australia have done well in the first hour of the chase! They have lost Finch but nothing worrying since then. Smith and Warner look calm and looks like an easy win for the hosts from here on. Still, a long way to go and Zimbabwe need to be sharper and need wickets to make things interesting. Also, Sikandar Raza is into the attack.
Again nips back in, on a length and outside off. Smith shoulders arms to it. That was tight.
Outside off. Left alone.
On middle. Blocked out.
This one jags back in, shorter and on off. Smith taps it in front of covers and Warner was looking for a quick single. Smith shouts 'Nooo' and Warner gets back in on time.
This is full and on middle. Smith drives it firmly but straight to mid on.
Length ball, outside off. Warner guides it to third man for one more.
Leg bye! A length ball, straight on the pads. Warner tucks it off the pads and to square leg. A leg bye is given.
Wide! A bouncer from Evans on middle. Warner sits under it. A wide is given.
On middle. Blocked out.
A single as this is hit through square leg.
Outside off, punched to covers.
That just swung away! Shorter and outside off, it lands and moves away sharply. Smith leaves it alone.
Short in length and on middle, pulled away to deep mid-wicket for a single.
On middle, it is hit to fine leg for one.
On middle, nudged to deep square leg for a single.
In the air and falls safe! Too full and outside off. Warner tries to heave across but slices it high and over mid off for a single.
Another easy leave by Warner.
Short of a length and around off. Warner leaves it alone.
A fuller ball, outside off. Warner is a bit late as he tries to push.
Full and on off. Smith stays back and defends.
Around off, nudged to mid-wicket.
Very full and on middle. Smith jams it to mid-wicket who parries it away and gives an extra run.
Shorter and outside off. Left alone.
Short in length and outside off. Smith tries to drive on the up but misses.
On a length and on middle. Smith tickles it to fine leg for a brace.
On a length and on off. Warner gets on his toes as he defends on the off side.
Shorter and outside off. Warner pushes it to point.
Wide! Bowls a short one on middle. Warner ducks under it. A wide is given.
Pitched up, outside off, driven to covers.
Fuller again, angling on middle. Defended.
Full and on middle. Blocked out.
Length ball, outside off. Warner swings and misses.
Length ball, outside off, easily left again.
On a length and on middle, late movement. Smith keeps it out.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Beautiful shot yet again! Already his third boundary! He already looks in fine touch! Overpitched, around off. Smith drives it past the bowler for four.
FOUR! Well played! Length ball, outside off. Smith whacks it across to deep mid-wicket for a boundary. Smith makes it look so easy.
On a length and outside off. Warner looks to defend but gets a thick outside edge to third man for one.
Powerplay 2! Now, four fielders will be allowed outside the inner circle till the 40th over.
A single to end the Powerplay! Full and on middle, drilled to mid on for a quick single. 50 up!
Short of a length and outside off. Warner looks to pull but miscues it to covers.
On the pads, flicked to mid-wicket.
Third dot! Length and on off. Warner punches it to covers.
Full and on off. Warner wrists to mid-wicket.
Length ball, outside off. Warner looks to defend but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Full and on off, pushed back to the bowler.
Around off. Defended out.
Beaten! Lovely bowling! On a length and outside off, jags away. Smith looks to defend inside the line and misses.
Full and on off. Smith nudges it straight to mid-wicket.

Wide! A length ball, angling down the leg side. Smith misses his flick.
On a length and on middle. Blocked to cover.
Smith is off the mark. Length and outside off. Smith splices it to third man for a single.

A length ball, outside off. Finch has a feel for it and gets beaten on the outside edge.

Outside off. Left alone.

Beaten! Short in length and around off. Warner is beaten on the outside edge as he tries to defend.

Short and outside off, not played at.
Fuller and on middle, Warner pushes it to mid on.

Two! On the pads, this is worked through square leg for two.
Length delivery, outside off, Warner watches it go to the keeper.
A single now as this is pushed towards cover.
Shorter and on off, this is cut to point.
Length and on off, Warner guides it to point.
Short and on the body, this is pulled down to fine leg for one.
On middle, kept out.
Back of a length and on off, defended.
Shorter and outside off, Finch looks to cut but misses.

Who will bowl from the other end? It is Victor Nyauchi.

FOUR! What a start! A short ball, outside off. Finch cuts it through point for a boundary.
